subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool design now, or defer cross-gateway messaging to the broader federation/identity design tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733?
rationale: The PR adds new core config, model-facing tool parameters, and a security-sensitive Gateway-to-Gateway trust path; code review can identify defects, but maintainers need to choose the product/security boundary before a repair is safe.

options.title: Gate on federation design
options.body: Pause this branch as implementation input until maintainers settle the cross-gateway identity, auth, and bridge contract, then rework the PR against that decision.

options.title: Sponsor narrow peer map
options.body: Approve a limited `gateway.peers` design for session tools, then require allowlist/auth hardening, a rebase, tests, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Close in favor of design issue
options.body: Close this PR and keep the problem represented by the open canonical issue and broader federation FRD.

recommendation.title: Gate on federation design
recommendation.body: Pause this branch as implementation input until maintainers settle the cross-gateway identity, auth, and bridge contract, then rework the PR against that decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history ties together sessions tools, `sessions.resolve`, and gatewayUrl security hardening.
